judged_text: The embed retrieval is fire-and-forget: the controller enqueues RetrieveTopic and renders 'loading', whose only follow-up is a 30-second document.location.reload() in app/views/embed/loading.html.erb, so an import that can never succeed leaves the visitor in an endless reload loop with no error state ever rendered. A user on a page whose import fails (dead/moved embed_url, fetch error, unparseable content, DB rejection) sees 'Loading Discussion...' reload every 30 seconds indefinitely — each cycle re-enqueues a job and re-queries the DB — while neither the end user nor the operator gets a surfaced failure; the only trace is buried Sidekiq error entries, and the 60s Redis throttle key claimed by the first failed attempt (lib/topic_retriever.rb:26-28) makes intermediate reloads no-op 'successfully' before the loop retries.

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds a loading flow with no terminal failure state: `EmbedController#best` enqueues `Jobs.enqueue(:retrieve_topic, ...)` and renders `app/views/embed/loading.html.erb` whenever `TopicEmbed.topic_id_for_embed(embed_url)` returns nil. The loading view unconditionally runs `setTimeout(function(){ document.location.reload(); }, 30000);`, so if retrieval/import never results in a `TopicEmbed` row (e.g., network/parsing failure in `TopicEmbed.import_remote` / `TopicRetriever#fetch_http`, or a permanent mismatch), the iframe will reload forever and keep re-hitting `embed#best`. Each reload re-enqueues `RetrieveTopic` again; the 60s Redis throttle in `TopicRetriever#retrieved_recently?` only reduces work inside the job, not the repeated enqueues or the endless reload UX.
